Director blessed our engagement. We are grateful that every step was guided by prayer and by people who truly cared.

stories.story: Both of us were working outside Kerala and hardly had time to meet families. The verified profiles gave our parents confidence, and the chat helped us know each other before the first family visit. We completed the pre-marriage course together and were married in our home parish.

articles.title: Building a Christ-Centered Marriage
articles.summary: Why prayer, forgiveness and shared purpose are the foundations of a lasting Catholic marriage.
body: A Christ-centered marriage is not a marriage without difficulties; it is a marriage where both spouses keep turning towards God together, especially in difficult moments.
Begin with small habits: a short prayer together before sleep, Sunday Mass as a family, and blessing each other before leaving home. These simple routines become anchors when life gets busy.
Forgiveness is the daily bread of married life. Learn to say ‘I am sorry’ and ‘I forgive you’ quickly, and never let the sun go down on your anger (Ephesians 4:26).
Finally, remember that marriage is a vocation of service. When each spouse seeks the good of the other, Christ becomes the third strand that keeps the cord from breaking (Ecclesiastes 4:12).

articles.title: The Beauty of a Catholic Family
articles.summary: The family as a ‘domestic church’ – a place where faith is first lived and learned.
body: The Church calls the family the ‘domestic church’. It is in the home that children first learn to pray, to forgive and to share.
Family prayer need not be long. A decade of the Rosary, reading the Sunday Gospel together, or thanking God for the day at dinner can shape a child's heart for life.
Grandparents are a treasure: their stories of faith, sacrifice and trust in God connect the younger generation to the roots of our Kerala Catholic heritage.
A Catholic family is also a family that serves – visiting the sick in the parish, supporting a neighbour, or joining a ward prayer group.

articles.title: Communication in Marriage
articles.summary: Practical ways to listen, speak kindly and resolve disagreements as a couple.
body: Most conflicts in marriage are not about money or in-laws – they are about not feeling heard. Listening is the first gift we give our spouse.
Try the ‘speaker–listener’ practice: one person speaks briefly, the other repeats back what they understood before replying.
Choose the right time. Important conversations go better after a meal and a prayer than at the end of a tiring day.
Keep a weekly ‘couple time’ – a walk, a cup of tea, or a visit to the church – where you simply talk about your hopes and worries.

articles.title: Preparing for Marriage: The Pre-Marriage Course
articles.summary: What to expect from the pre-marriage course and why couples should attend it early.
body: The pre-marriage course is a time for the couple to reflect on the sacrament they are about to receive, guided by priests, doctors, counsellors and married couples.
Sessions usually cover the theology of marriage, communication, family finances, natural family planning and the responsibilities of parenting.
Attend the course soon after the engagement is fixed – not in the last week before the wedding – so there is time to discuss what you learn.
Contact the Family Apostolate office for the schedule of upcoming courses and registration details.

articles.title: Choosing a Life Partner with Prayer
articles.summary: Discernment tips for young Catholics who are looking for a spouse.
body: Choosing a life partner is one of the most important decisions of life. Bring it to prayer before, during and after you meet someone.
Look for shared values more than shared hobbies: faith, honesty, kindness and a willingness to grow.
Involve your parents and a trusted priest early. Their experience can help you see what you might miss.
Be patient. As the Psalm says, ‘Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage’ (Psalm 27:14).

articles.title: Staying Safe While Finding Your Match
articles.summary: Simple safety guidelines for members of the Family Apostolate matrimony platform.
body: Never share bank details, OTPs or send money to anyone you meet online, even if the request seems urgent.
Keep early conversations on the platform and involve your families before meeting in person.
Meet in a public place or at home in the presence of elders, and inform a family member before you go.
If anything feels wrong, use the ‘Report Profile’ option or contact the Family Apostolate office immediately.
